form.quantity: Ratio of honey volume stored per unit wax mass in hexagonal cells compared to the next-best regular tessellation. Derives from the honeycomb conjecture: hexagons minimize total perimeter for equal-area tiling of a plane.

process_forms.driver: F_FLOW (D0_law, CONTESTED): Cells are built circular; visco-elastic wax heated by workers flows near triple junctions; surface-energy minimization straightens walls into rounded hexagons. Heat: E_BODY_HEAT (D1_energy, TRACED).

driver_nodes.claim: Cells are built circular; visco-elastic wax heated by workers flows near triple junctions; surface-energy minimization straightens walls into rounded hexagons.
Heat for wax working and brood comes from worker thoracic muscle metabolism fuelled by nectar sugar; ~40% of the colony's annual energy intake goes to brood-nest heating.
Workers heat the wax with their bodies during comb building.

timescale.text: ≈6 s fully heated; ≈36 s partially heated
timescale.note: cycle context as recorded: comb building, wax ~45 °C. The cycle is the formation transient; the periods of the enclosing cycles are in registry/cycles.json.

regime.note: Lower bound 45 °C is 'about'; treat as CONDITIONAL until a source gives a range. | v0.3 (2026-11-24): the 45 °C lower bound comes from C_FLOW_T, now CONTESTED; the regime is CONDITIONAL on which account holds. Bauer & Bienefeld's 33.6–37.6 °C would fall below this bound.
